title: Iman Gadzhi on building from nothing: patience, risk management, and playing the long game
summary: Iman Gadzhi walks through his path from a 95-pound-a-week social media client to a multi-company empire. He covers patience through a seven-month drought, contractor arbitrage, a 70/30 YouTube content split, and why he never sells hard. He also names the five skills he values most and admits his pricing mistake.

principles.text: Don't compare yourself to others while you're building; focus on your own progress and be patient through the slow early phase.
principles.quote: I didn't look around I just looked at myself and I realized listen I got to be patient this stuff takes time this stuff takes time to learn these skills and also what's my other option

principles.text: Split YouTube content 70/30: most videos to reach new audiences, the rest to retain existing fans.
principles.quote: 70% of my videos is to grow new audience and the other 30% of my videos is the stuff that I know my audience loves and would make sure that they don't unsubscribe

principles.text: Constantly A/B test thumbnails on old videos to keep subscriber growth going without new uploads.
principles.quote: every single day we would rehash an old YouTube video so we would go back and we would uh and once again there's 15 options so we would go back and we would AB split test old videos

principles.text: Use global contractor arbitrage: pay talented people in cheaper markets per client while charging Western clients full rates.
principles.quote: I could start using contractor Arbitrage I could start using this Global Market that we have

principles.text: Sell rarely to protect longevity and brand trust; avoid sponsorships and constant promotion.
principles.quote: I literally sell something twice a year that's it there's two weeks in the year that I sell the rest of year I don't sell I don't do any sponsored posts

principles.text: Practice risk management: don't tell beginners to gamble on crypto; choose paths where failure costs little and skills compound.
principles.quote: you need to work on businesses and you need to work on things where even if you fail for 12 months how much damage is that going to cause to you
